details.scope: Complete active base config document before the write

details.scope_guard: Only preset.effort and preset.reasoning_effort may change.

change_summary.expected_result: The active base configuration has no preset effort or reasoning_effort for the five current model specs. With those fields absent, the provider chooses its own default. The future client control may send an effort only for the current conversation and never writes the global model spec.
functions: Read exactly one active role/__base__ config and exactly one spec for each of the five named models.
Back up the complete base config in codexConfigBackups before the first write.
Remove only preset.effort and preset.reasoning_effort, increment configVersion, and verify the persisted post-state.
Provide an idempotent, backup-id guarded rollback runner without restarting any service.
limitations: This operation changes the global active base model specs only; existing conversation documents are not rewritten.
The client-side session-only effort selector is a separate development change and is not deployed by this data operation.
No billable model request is required for acceptance.
change_summary.reason: The current five model specs contain vendor-specific preset reasoning values (none and high), which prevents the provider from selecting its own automatic default and conflicts with the requested per-conversation control.
change_summary.risk: A broad Mongo update could change model routing or unrelated configuration. The operation uses exact model names, a complete pre-write backup, config version guard through the active base document, post-write assertions, and a data-only target lock.

details.method: Before the first Mongo write, the runner stores the complete active base config in codexConfigBackups with the unique backup_id clear-model-effort-<source>-<utc timestamp>. remote-rollback.sh restores that exact document and verifies the post-rollback snapshot.

details.first_failed_attempt: The initial runner stopped before write because the mode variable was not passed into docker exec; the corrected runner was packaged and the successful attempt created the backup above.
